switch Statements and Expressions

Stage 3 Demo ⏱ 14 min 📖 Glossary

switch is a mail sorter: ONE value glides in, exactly ONE labeled slot accepts it. Cleaner than six else-ifs when a single thing meets many fixed constants.

🔎 Motivating questionWhy do post offices sort by pincode instead of reading every letter completely?

Objectives

  • Write switch with break
  • Use arrow -> form
  • Choose switch vs if

Needs first: Nested Conditions

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

The pincode sorter. It glances at ONE code and slides the letter into exactly one slot; the DEFAULT slot catches unknown codes. Forget break in the old style and the letter slides into the NEXT slot too (fall-through) — chaos.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: sorters only match exact LABELS (numbers, strings, enums). A “taller than 180 cm” range cannot be a slot — ranges need if-else.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Classic form: switch (day) { case 1: ...; break; case 2: ...; break; default: ...; }. Each break STOPS the slide; without it, execution falls through into the next case.

Modern arrow form (Java 14+): case 1 -> "Monday"; — no break needed, no fall-through possible. As an EXPRESSION it can also produce a value, like below.

Use switch for fixed choices: days, menu numbers, grade letters, enum values. Use if-else for ranges, booleans, and float comparisons.

Always write default: unknown inputs must land somewhere visible, never vanish silently.

⚙️ Tech details — precise facts
  • switch accepts int, char, String, enums (plus byte/short and wrappers). long, float, double, boolean are REJECTED — the compiler says so.
  • Arrow switches can be exhaustive expressions: String s = switch (day) { case 1 -> "Mon"; ... default -> "?"; }; — semicolon and all.
  • String cases use .equals content matching internally (plus null throws NullPointerException — yes, switch on null crashes).

3 Watch it move: Mail sorter

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
public class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    int day = 3;
    String name = switch (day) {
      case 1 -> "Monday";
      case 2 -> "Tuesday";
      case 3 -> "Wednesday";
      default -> "Unknown day";
    };
    System.out.println(name);
    System.out.println("Day " + day + " done");
  }
}
▶ Output Wednesday Day 3 done
  • day = 3 matches exactly one arrow.
  • Arrow form needs no break and yields a value.
  • default catches every other number.
▶️ Run it yourselfSave exactly as Main.java, then javac Main.java and java Main. Every full program in this course works this way.
💡 Why this output?Exact label match on 3; the switch expression hands back "Wednesday"; default never fires.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: Missing break in the old colon style.Why: Execution FALLS THROUGH into the next case — two slots “accept” one letter.
✅ Fix: Add break; to every case — or switch to the arrow form.
❌ Mistake 2: switch (score > 90) or switch (3.5).Why: Boolean ranges and doubles are not sortable labels — rejected.
✅ Fix: Ranges belong to if-else; doubles to comparisons.
❌ Mistake 3: No default, unknown input arrives.Why: Silence: nothing runs, nothing explains. Debugging nightmare.
✅ Fix: Always add default — even if it just complains loudly.

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Build a menu switch

choice 1 → “Idli”, 2 → “Dosa”, anything else → “Pick 1 or 2”. Arrow style.

HintTwo arrows plus default.
SolutionString food = switch (choice) { case 1 -> "Idli"; case 2 -> "Dosa"; default -> "Pick 1 or 2"; };
Spot the fall-through

Colon style, no breaks: case 1: a(); case 2: b(); — day = 1 runs what?

HintNothing stops the slide.
SolutionBOTH a() and b(). Add break; after each.

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • One value, many exact labels.
  • Arrow form kills fall-through; colon form needs break.
  • Always write default.
  • Ranges and doubles belong to if-else.
🧠 Recall challengeWhen do you reach for switch instead of if-else?
